class.name: UZUUI
class.brief_description: A UI kit: procedural panels, a matching theme, and constructors for common parts.
class.description: [UZUUI] gives a game UI a finished look without drawn assets. Panels are drawn procedurally, each as one 9-slice image: a vertical gradient, rounded corners, a border and a soft shadow. [method create_theme] styles every common control with them: panels, buttons (normal, hover, pressed, disabled), bars, tabs, lists and tooltips. The [code]make_*[/code] methods build the usual parts. [codeblock] var screen = Control.new() screen.theme = UZUUI.create_theme({"accent": "#d9a441", "font_size": 20}) var dialog = UZUUI.make_dialog("Elder", "Bring three shards.", ["Accept", "Later"]) screen.add_child(dialog) [/codeblock] Screens can also be built from a JSON spec with [code]ai_loop/uzu.py ui[/code], which uses this class. World themes ([method create_world_theme]) give game frames instead of plain panels: wood, parchment, glass, halftone and other textures, game shapes and corner ornaments, and the classic game parts (segmented gauges, talk windows, item slots, ribbons). One name switches the world. [b]Note:[/b] This class is specific to U.ZU Engine.

method.name: create_frame_style
method.description: Returns a 9-slice style from [method draw_frame]. Its middle repeats, so the texture keeps its scale at any size. The shadow is drawn outside the control's rectangle. Lengths follow the layout scale (see [method get_layout_scale]): [code]shadow[/code] snaps to an elevation level (or name the level with [code]elevation[/code]), [code]radius[/code] snaps to the radius scale, and [code]padding[/code] is a spacing step — a number, snapped, or a step name ([code]"xs"[/code], [code]"s"[/code], [code]"m"[/code], [code]"l"[/code], [code]"xl"[/code], [code]"xxl"[/code]).

method.name: create_panel_style
method.description: Returns a panel style. Keys (colors are [Color] or [code]"#rrggbb[aa]"[/code]): - [code]bg[/code], or [code]top[/code] and [code]bottom[/code] for a vertical gradient. - [code]radius[/code]: the corner radius (snapped to the layout scale's radius steps). - [code]border[/code] and [code]border_width[/code]. - [code]shadow[/code]: the shadow size, drawn outside the control's rectangle; snapped to an elevation level of the layout scale. [code]elevation[/code] (0 to 4) names the level instead. - [code]padding[/code]: the content margin; a spacing step of the layout scale, as a number (snapped) or a step name ([code]"xs"[/code] to [code]"xxl"[/code]).

method.name: create_theme
method.description: Returns a theme for the common controls. All keys are optional (see [method get_theme_defaults]): - [code]accent[/code]: borders and the bar fill. - [code]text[/code]: the text color. - [code]font[/code] (a [Font]) and [code]font_size[/code] (also the base size of the type scale; see [method get_type_scale]). - [code]panel[/code], [code]button[/code] and [code]bar[/code]: style dictionaries as in [method create_panel_style]. Buttons also take [code]hover[/code] and [code]pressed[/code] colors; bars take [code]fill[/code].

method.name: create_world_material
method.description: Returns the moving decoration of a world's frames: a canvas shader that glints (fantasy, wafu, persona), flows with scan lines (sf), flickers (horror), or blinks in steps (pixel). [UZUUIWorld] puts it on the frames. The decoration is masked by the frame texture's alpha, so it stays on the frame's body and never whitens the drop shadow or the background (B-1319). Returns [code]null[/code] for an unknown world.

method.name: draw_backdrop
method.description: Generates a screen backdrop (B-1319): a composed background, never a flat fill. Style keys: [code]"size"[/code] (default 1152×648), [code]"base"[/code], [code]"mottle"[/code] (0..1 fbm variation), [code]"band"[/code] (a diagonal band's color; absent for no band), [code]"band_y"[/code], [code]"band_h"[/code], [code]"band_halftone"[/code], [code]"band_slope"[/code], [code]"band_under"[/code] / [code]"band_under_h"[/code] (a dark under-band), [code]"band2"[/code] / [code]"band2_y"[/code] / [code]"band2_h"[/code] / [code]"band2_slope"[/code] / [code]"band2_halftone"[/code] (a second, crossing band, B-1320), [code]"line"[/code] (a thin line along the band's upper edge), [code]"glow"[/code] / [code]"glow_pos"[/code] / [code]"glow_strength"[/code] and [code]"glow2"[/code] / [code]"glow2_pos"[/code] / [code]"glow2_strength"[/code] (soft radial glows), [code]"stars"[/code] / [code]"star"[/code] (four-point sparkles over the upper field, B-1320), [code]"vignette"[/code] (0..1 edge darkening), [code]"seed"[/code], [code]"gradient_to"[/code] / [code]"gradient_dir"[/code] (a colour run under the ground, B-1321) with [code]"gradient_stops"[/code] / [code]"gradient_center"[/code] / [code]"gradient_radius"[/code] (multi-stop and radial runs, B-1322), [code]"band_gradient_to"[/code] / [code]"band_gradient_stops"[/code] (the band's own run across its width), [code]"halftone_cells"[/code] / [code]"halftone_dot"[/code] (the bands' halftone print: pitch in cells per tile, and the dots' ink). A world's button options may also name [code]"invert"[/code] / [code]"invert_text"[/code]: the button bar flips to that color on hover and focus instead of lightening (persona's red slash, B-1320).

method.name: get_backdrop_options
method.description: Returns a world's backdrop composition for [method draw_backdrop] (see [method get_world_names]). Empty for an unknown world.

method.name: make_backdrop
method.description: Builds a world's backdrop as a full-rect [TextureRect] (aspect-covered, mouse-transparent), ready to add as a screen's first child. Returns [code]null[/code] for an unknown world.

method.name: create_world_theme
method.description: Returns the theme of a world (see [method get_world_names]): textured frames for panels, buttons, tabs, lists and tooltips, the world's colors, and the type variations of the game parts ([code]UZUGauge[/code], [code]UZUTalk[/code], [code]UZUNameTag[/code], [code]UZUSlot[/code], [code]UZURibbon[/code]). So the same UI changes world with one name. [param overrides] changes any option of [method get_world_options], for example [code]font[/code]. The theme's metadata holds [code]uzu_world[/code] and [code]uzu_motion[/code] ([method get_world_motion]). Returns [code]null[/code] for an unknown world.

method.name: draw_frame
method.description: Draws the 9-slice image of a game frame. Keys: - [code]material[/code]: [code]wood[/code], [code]metal[/code], [code]parchment[/code], [code]stone[/code], [code]glass[/code], [code]halftone[/code], [code]grime[/code] or [code]flat[/code]. - [code]shape[/code]: [code]rounded[/code], [code]chamfer[/code], [code]skew[/code] or [code]pixel[/code]. Pixel frames have hard edges with no anti-aliasing. - [code]base[/code], [code]edge[/code] and [code]accent[/code] colors. - [code]radius[/code], [code]border_width[/code] and [code]shadow[/code]. - [code]ornament[/code]: corner ornaments, [code]none[/code], [code]rivets[/code], [code]nails[/code], [code]brackets[/code] or [code]diamonds[/code]. - [code]padding[/code] and [code]seed[/code]. - [code]scale[/code]: generation resolution, 1 (default) or 2 (twice the px, for high-DPI). - [code]inner_shadow[/code], [code]highlight[/code] and [code]glow[/code]: depth layers over the material, each 0..1 (B-1318). The inner shadow shades the surface just inside the rim, the highlight is the rim light from the top left, and the glow bleeds the accent color in from the edge. All default to off, except the [code]glow[/code] of [code]glass[/code], which has always had one (0.35). - [code]gradient_to[/code] and [code]gradient_dir[/code]: a colour run under the material, from [code]base[/code] to the named colour along [code]down[/code] (default), [code]up[/code], [code]left[/code] or [code]right[/code] (B-1321). The axis it runs along stretches instead of tiling, so the run spans the panel exactly once. - [code]gradient_stops[/code]: the run's remaining stops as an Array of colors, evenly spaced after [code]base[/code] — three stops and more, so a surface can be lit, full and shaded in one run (B-1322). [code]gradient_dir[/code] also takes [code]radial[/code]: the run measures distance from [code]gradient_center[/code] (0..1, default the middle) and reaches the last stop at [code]gradient_radius[/code] (a fraction of the longer side, default 0.75). - [code]halftone_cells[/code] and [code]halftone_dot[/code]: the halftone print's pitch in cells per tile (default 32, an 8 px cell; persona prints 64, a 4 px cell) and the dots' ink colour (B-1321). Unset, the ink is the ground darkened toward black; a shade of the ground — a maroon on persona's red — reads as print instead of holes. The textures are procedural and repeat every 32 pixels.

method.name: draw_panel
method.description: Draws the 9-slice image of a panel. This is what [method create_panel_style] uses.

method.name: get_layout_scale
method.description: Returns the layout scale every length in a theme comes from: [code]spacing[/code] (content margins and separations, in px), [code]radius[/code] (corner radii), [code]spacing_steps[/code] (the step names [code]"xs"[/code] to [code]"xxl"[/code] and their px), and [code]elevation[/code] (levels [code]"0"[/code] to [code]"4"[/code], each a shadow triple of [code]shadow[/code] size, [code]offset_y[/code] drop and [code]alpha[/code]). The same Dictionary is stored in every theme's [code]uzu_layout[/code] metadata.

method.name: get_theme_defaults
method.description: Returns the default options of [method create_theme].

method.name: get_type_scale
method.description: Returns the type scale for a base font size: five named text steps — [code]display[/code], [code]title[/code], [code]heading[/code], [code]body[/code], [code]caption[/code] — on a modular scale with ratio 1.25 ([code]body[/code] is the base size itself). Each step is a Dictionary with [code]size[/code], [code]line_spacing[/code], [code]letter_spacing[/code] (pixels of glyph tracking), [code]outline_size[/code] and [code]shadow_offset[/code] (the step's decoration preset), and [code]variation[/code]: the [Label] type variation every theme created by [method create_theme] and [method create_world_theme] carries for the step. The same Dictionary is stored in the theme's [code]uzu_type_scale[/code] metadata.

method.name: get_world_motion
method.description: Returns how a world's UI moves when opened or hovered: [code]duration[/code], [code]transition[/code], [code]ease[/code], [code]overshoot[/code] and [code]steps[/code]. Persona-like UI snaps with a big overshoot, sf UI eases in mechanically, fantasy UI has a soft overshoot, and pixel UI steps frame by frame.

method.name: get_world_names
method.description: Returns the world themes: [code]fantasy[/code], [code]wafu[/code], [code]sf[/code], [code]horror[/code], [code]persona[/code] and [code]pixel[/code].

method.name: get_world_options
method.description: Returns the options of a world: [code]frame[/code] and [code]button[/code] (frame styles), [code]text[/code], [code]button_text[/code], [code]accent[/code], [code]fill[/code] and [code]font_size[/code].

method.name: make_bar
method.description: Returns a [ProgressBar] without the percentage text.

method.name: make_button
method.description: Returns a [Button].

method.name: make_dialog
method.description: Returns a panel with a title, wrapped text, and a row of buttons on the right. The parts are [code]Content/Title[/code], [code]Content/Text[/code] and [code]Content/Buttons/<label>[/code].

method.name: make_gauge
method.description: Returns a segmented gauge: a [ProgressBar] whose fill is a row of segments. It is 12 pixels per segment wide.

method.name: make_item_slot
method.description: Returns a square, sunken item slot with a label, and a count in the corner when [param count] is above 0.

method.name: make_label
method.description: Returns a [Label] in one step of the type scale ([code]display[/code], [code]title[/code], [code]heading[/code], [code]body[/code] or [code]caption[/code]; see [method get_type_scale]): the label carries the step's type variation, so the theme it ends up under gives it the step's size, line and letter spacing, and decoration. An unknown step is treated as [code]body[/code].

method.name: make_list
method.description: Returns an [ItemList] with the items, as tall as its content.

method.name: make_panel
method.description: Returns a [PanelContainer], holding [param content] if given.

method.name: make_ribbon
method.description: Returns a ribbon heading in the world's accent color.

method.name: make_separator
method.description: Returns a decorated divider: a line that fades at both ends, with a diamond in the middle.

method.name: get_skew_safe_margins
method.description: Returns the slant of a frame style as [code]{"slope": float, "travel": float}[/code] (zeroes unless the style's shape is [code]skew[/code]). A skew parallelogram leans with height, so across the frame its edge travels [code]travel[/code] px horizontally: content whose bottom row sits at fraction [code]f[/code] of the panel's height needs [code]travel * f[/code] of extra left inset to stay inside the shape, and content whose top row sits at fraction [code]f'[/code] needs [code]travel * (1 - f')[/code] on the right. Layouts and the containment check (B-1315) use this instead of eyeballing the slant.

method.name: make_touch_button
method.description: Returns a round pad [Button] for touch layouts, carrying the theme's [code]UZUTouchButton[/code] type variation (drawn disc faces for every state), so it follows the world theme like any other part.

method.name: make_touch_stick
method.description: Returns a [UZUTouchStick]: a virtual analog stick for touch layouts, drawn from the theme's [code]UZUTouchStick[/code] colours. The stick reports its value through [signal UZUTouchStick.value_changed]; feeding input actions from it is the game's job.

method.name: make_tabs
method.description: Returns a [TabContainer] with one empty page (a [VBoxContainer]) per title.

method.name: make_talk_window
method.description: Returns a talk window: a name tag over the window's top edge ([code]TagMargin/NameTag/Speaker[/code]), the line ([code]Window/Body/Line[/code]), and a next mark ([code]Window/Body/Next[/code]).
